thesis: This episode argues that the most significant real estate and technology investment opportunities lie in the repurposing of industrial buildings for food delivery (Cloud Kitchens) and the construction of infill industrial centers to support Amazon's logistics network. The speaker also highlights the growing institutional interest in mobile home parks and single-family home acquisitions as a shift in the housing market.

claims.claim: The speaker likes Travis Kalanick's Cloud Kitchen concept as an amazing real estate play involving buying and repurposing industrial buildings for commercial kitchens.
claims.quote: Another one is I like what Travis Kalanick and Uber is up to. He has something called Cloud Kitchen, which I think is an amazing real estate play. So he's building, he's buying and repurposing industrial buildings.

claims.claim: The speaker believes Cloud Kitchen is a technology play leveraging Uber's network to locate kitchens based on demand for food delivery.
claims.quote: And it's a technology play because he's in, I think he sort of is in with like the Postmates and the Uber Eats of the World where he knows where everyone's pinging to get these food, essentially.

claims.claim: The speaker thinks restaurants can thrive on delivery platforms without a physical location, creating a huge market for this model.
claims.quote: And in restaurants nowadays, you don't even have to have to have a physical location. You could be built on these platforms and create a thriving business. I believe the next McDonald's, the next large, huge restaurateur is going to be built upon just. delivery and not having a physical footprint.

claims.claim: The speaker sees a huge market for food delivery technology and believes this trend will continue.
claims.quote: I think there's a huge market for that and you're going to continue seeing that, you know, technology with food delivery.

claims.claim: The speaker believes Amazon has an unsatiable demand for more infill industrial centers to deliver goods quickly.
claims.quote: Like, you know, Amazon has an unsatiable demand for more and more infill centers that could deliver within like an hour or less goods. So I'd say buying industrial infill, it's sort of expensive now, but if you believe that there's going to just be more and more demand for people to get goods quickly, you have the Omna Channel retailers.
